text: When designing REST APIs, following best practices helps developers use your service easily. First, choose clear and meaningful names for your endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so other developers understand what each resource does. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation is also essential because it explains how each endpoint works and what data it expects. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so older applications continue to work when you make changes. These simple rules make your API reliable and easier to maintain.
